2:13|The project (mwaskom, checked out at an old commit) has this issue:
3:00|
4:e8|Wrong legend values of large ranges
5:1f|As of 0.12.1, legends describing large numbers that were created using `ScalarFormatter` with an offset are formatted without their multiplicative offset value. An example:
6:4f|```python
7:ce|import seaborn as sns
8:c4|import seaborn.objects as so
9:00|
10:26|penguins = sns.load_dataset("Penguins")
11:56|penguins["body_mass_mg"] = penguins["body_mass_g"]*1000
12:77|(
13:6f|    so.Plot(
14:bc|        penguins, x="bill_length_mm", y="bill_depth_mm",
15:7c|        color="species", pointsize="body_mass_mg",
16:09|    )
17:3a|    .add(so.Dot())
18:e1|)
19:cd|```
20:b5|The code creates the following plot:
21:e2|![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13831112/205512305-778966db-f8d8-43f3-a2c0-5e5ce95bae39.png)
22:e5|which is wrong because `body_mass_mg` is in the order of 1E6. The issue also reproduces if you create the mentioned plot using `scatterplot`.
23:45| 
24:d9|I believe the issue stems from not using the offset value of the `ScalarFormatter` used to generate the tick labels:
25:3e|https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn/blob/ba786bc14eb255f6b4fb7619c8210c5a8016a26f/seaborn/_core/scales.py#L377-L382
26:b2|Examining the code of `ScalarFormatter` suggests the issue also depends on the following rcParam settings:
27:0b|`mpl.rcParams['axes.formatter.useoffset']`
28:ad|`mpl.rcParams['axes.formatter.offset_threshold']`
29:c9|However, I did not test it. 
30:00|
31:4d|The offset value can be safely retrieved from all formatters and based on that it can be used to create the legend title and/or labels.
32:00|
33:00|
34:ab|Find the cause and make the minimal correct fix in the source (not in tests).
35:07|Do NOT modify or add tests. Do NOT commit. Leave your changes in the working tree.

def locator_to_legend_entries(locator, limits, dtype):
    """Return levels and formatted levels for brief numeric legends."""
    raw_levels = locator.tick_values(*limits).astype(dtype)

    # The locator can return ticks outside the limits, clip them here
    raw_levels = [l for l in raw_levels if l >= limits[0] and l <= limits[1]]

    class dummy_axis:

def locator_to_legend_entries(locator, limits, dtype):
    """Return levels and formatted levels for brief numeric legends."""
    raw_levels = locator.tick_values(*limits).astype(dtype)
